substrate_text: This substrate runs 3D linear-elastic isotropic small-deflection static cantilever beams: a rectangular prism clamped on one end face, loaded by a single transverse force distributed over the opposite end face. The solver is FEniCSx / DOLFINx 0.11.0.post0 (real-mode PETSc, float64) running inside the dolfinx-prod container, driven through the run_fenicsx wrapper -- deterministic Python with no AI inside, which meshes the beam, solves one linear system, and reads the result. This is FEniCSx (import dolfinx), NOT legacy FEniCS (from dolfin import), which last released in 2019 and does not run here. | The element is Lagrange (continuous, vector-valued) of a degree the CASE chooses: element_degree is typed input, not a fixed property of the instrument. That choice is a physics decision, not a preference -- see the honest limits. | The wrapper honors exactly these canonical parameter names; anything else is rejected by name, and every one is REQUIRED (there are no defaults -- an omitted field is a rejection, never a guess): - length (m) -- beam length, spanning X; clamped at x=0 - width (m) -- section width, spanning Y - height (m) -- section height, spanning Z; the load direction - E (Pa) -- Young's modulus; must be positive - nu (-) -- Poisson's ratio; must be in (-1, 0.5) - tip_load (N) -- total transverse load at x=length, in -Z, distributed uniformly over the tip face - mesh_density (int) -- hexahedral element count along the length; the width and height counts scale by aspect ratio, so the reference beam meshes 8 -> 8x1x1, 16 -> 16x1x1, 32 -> 32x2x2 - element_degree (int) -- Lagrange polynomial degree; >= 1 accepted, >= 2 validated. See the honest limits: this field is the difference between a trustworthy number and a confident wrong one. The first seven names carry the SAME units and semantics as the sibling CalculiX cantilever family v1, deliberately, so one beam can be posed to both instruments; element_degree is this family's own and has no CalculiX counterpart (that solver's C3D8I incompatible-modes element fixes locking in the element formulation instead, which is why it has no such knob).
envelope_text: On a run that completes, a small fixed summary -- never the raw solver output: - valid: true or false. False whenever the input was rejected, the substrate was unreachable, the solve failed, or the output was unusable. - qoi (on a valid run), carrying BOTH of: * tip_displacement (m): the maximum |u_z| over the displacement field's degrees of freedom. For Lagrange elements these are point evaluations at the element's dof coordinates -- mesh nodes at degree 1, and nodes plus edge/face/interior points at degree 2 and above. * max_von_mises (Pa): the pointwise maximum von Mises stress, computed by interpolating the stress derived from the displacement into a discontinuous space of degree (element_degree - 1) and taking the maximum over that space's dofs. - diagnostics: a bounded human-readable string (solver version, element family and degree, mesh size, cell and dof counts, scalar type, solve time), capped at 800 characters. - runtime_s: wall-clock seconds. On any failure: valid=false, qoi=null, and diagnostics names the reason. The instrument NEVER fabricates a number. A run is killed after 600 seconds of wall-clock time and reported as a failure. | HONEST LIMITS - Linear-elastic isotropic small-deflection statics ONLY. There is no plasticity, no hyperelasticity, no contact, no buckling, no dynamics, no anisotropy, no thermal coupling. A case whose physics is actually any of those will still return a number, and the wrapper cannot detect that. - ELEMENT DEGREE IS A REGIME BOUNDARY, NOT A PREFERENCE. A fully-integrated degree-1 Lagrange hex SHEAR-LOCKS in bending: it reports a beam that is far too stiff. Measured on this substrate, on the reference beam: degree 1 returns 0.28x the closed-form tip deflection at mesh_density 8, and is still 5.5% too stiff at mesh_density 64, while degree 2 is within 1.31% at mesh_density 8. Degree 1 is ACCEPTED by the typed input and IS NOT an error the wrapper reports -- a degree-1 run converges cleanly and returns a confident, wrong number. Only degree >= 2 is validated. - Refinement does not rescue a locked element, and the reason matters: locking severity is governed by ELEMENT ASPECT RATIO, not element count. Measured: refining ONLY through the thickness (holding 8 elements along the length) moved degree 1 from 0.2800x to 0.2894x of the closed form -- essentially nothing, across an 8x increase in through-thickness elements. Refining along the length helps substantially but plateaus short of correct (0.86x at 128 elements along the length). Degree 2 needs neither: it sits at 0.987x on the very coarsest 8x1x1 mesh. - Shear locking (degree-1 bending stiffness; fixed by degree >= 2) and VOLUMETRIC locking (near-incompressibility as nu approaches 0.5) are two DIFFERENT diseases. Degree 2 does NOT fix volumetric locking; the remedies for that are mixed/u-p formulations, selective reduced integration, or F-bar, none of which this instrument has. A case with nu near 0.5 is numerically suspect even though the input is well-formed and the solve converges. - The Euler-Bernoulli closed form delta = P*L^3/(3*E*I) with I = w*h^3/12 is the only reference this instrument is validated against, and it is only itself trustworthy for SLENDER beams -- it neglects shear deformation, whose correction grows rapidly below length/height = 10. Note the tension honestly: the regime where the reference is most valid (slender) is the regime where a naive low-order element is most wrong. Both are true at once. - max_von_mises is REPORTED, NOT VALIDATED. Its pointwise maximum sits at the clamped-corner stress singularity, which belongs to the continuum problem itself: it rises with refinement instead of settling (measured at degree 2: 4.246e7 -> 4.492e7 -> 4.670e7 Pa across mesh_density 8 -> 16 -> 32) and has no converged value to find. At degree 1 it is additionally corrupted by its own extraction: the degree-0 sample points sit at cell centres, which on a one-element-thick mesh lie exactly on the beam's neutral axis where bending stress vanishes -- measured 6.93e5 Pa at 8x1x1 versus 5.80e6 Pa at 8x1x2, an 8x swing from a mesh change that should barely matter. - There is NO regime check anywhere in this instrument. It confirms that the solve ran and the output parsed -- never that the physics is in-regime, never that the mesh is converged, never that the element is appropriate. Slenderness, linearity, and locking are all invisible to it.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever beam, length 1.0 m, width 0.05 m, height 0.05 m (length/height = 20), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=1000 N, mesh_density=16, element_degree=2. Extract tip_displacement (the maximum transverse deflection).
gate_cases.note: The validated reference beam at the validated element degree. delta/L ~ 0.3%; slenderness 20; measured gap vs Euler-Bernoulli 0.61% at this mesh, well inside the 2% band.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the named linear-elastic small-deflection cantilever FE model, used as-is
gate_cases.label_rationale: Every card bound is satisfied with margin (G1 20>=10, G2 0.3%<=10%, G3 0.61%<=2%, G5 degree 2>=2) and the QoI is the validated one, so trust is the only defensible verdict.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever beam, length 2.0 m, width 0.05 m, height 0.05 m (length/height = 40), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=500 N, mesh_density=16, element_degree=2. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: Very slender (length/height = 40), small deflection (delta/L ~ 0.61%); deep inside G1 and G2 at the validated degree.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the named linear-elastic small-deflection cantilever FE model, used as-is
gate_cases.label_rationale: Slenderness 40 is where Euler-Bernoulli is MOST valid and degree 2 does not lock, so nothing on the card excludes trust.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever beam, length 1.0 m, width 0.05 m, height 0.05 m (length/height = 20), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=3300 N, mesh_density=8, element_degree=2. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: delta/L ~ 1.0% -- an order of magnitude below the G2 linearity bound but the largest deflection on the in-envelope slate, at the COARSEST mesh (measured gap 1.31%, inside the 2% G3 band but the closest in-envelope case to its edge).
gate_cases.right_instrument: the named linear-elastic small-deflection cantilever FE model, used as-is
gate_cases.label_rationale: In-envelope on every bound, but it approaches the G3 mesh-reproduction edge from the coarse side, so a gate asking for a finer mesh before trusting is defensible; refine is admitted alongside trust.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever beam, length 1.0 m, width 0.10 m, height 0.10 m (length/height = 10), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=2000 N, mesh_density=16, element_degree=2. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: length/height = 10 EXACTLY -- the G1 boundary, on the inside. delta/L ~ 0.038%. The closest in-envelope case to `out`.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the named linear-elastic small-deflection cantilever FE model, used as-is
gate_cases.label_rationale: G1 is stated as L/h >= 10 and this case satisfies it exactly; the bound is inclusive, so trust holds -- this case measures whether the gate reads the boundary as the card writes it.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever beam, length 1.0 m, width 0.05 m, height 0.05 m (length/height = 20), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=1000 N, mesh_density=16, element_degree=3. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: The reference beam at element_degree=3. The G5 bound is a FLOOR (degree >= 2), not an exact value: a higher degree is more accurate, not less eligible.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the named linear-elastic small-deflection cantilever FE model, used as-is
gate_cases.label_rationale: Tests that the gate reads G5 as a floor rather than as 'degree must equal 2'; a refine/defer here would mean the bound transmitted as an equality, which is a card-to-gate transmission finding.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever beam, length 1.0 m, width 0.05 m, height 0.05 m (length/height = 20), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=1000 N, mesh_density=32, element_degree=1. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: CONVERGED-BUT-WRONG, the middle zone. Fine mesh, clean solve, locked element: MEASURED 16.4% too stiff (0.8364x the closed form) -- well outside the 2% G3 band, with nothing in the diagnostics to say so.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the same FE model re-run at element_degree >= 2, which resolves bending without locking on this very mesh
gate_cases.label_rationale: G5 excludes trust for degree < 2; the fix is a re-run at a higher degree (refine) or routing to a non-locking instrument (defer). A 'trust' draw here is the dangerous false-trust error: the number is confident, clean, and 16% wrong.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever beam, length 1.0 m, width 0.05 m, height 0.05 m (length/height = 20), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=1000 N, mesh_density=64, element_degree=1. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: The HARDER locking case, deliberately. MEASURED only 5.5% too stiff (0.9446x) -- still outside the 2% G3 band and still a locked element, but the error is now small enough to look like ordinary discretization error rather than a regime violation.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the same FE model re-run at element_degree >= 2, which resolves bending without locking on this very mesh
gate_cases.label_rationale: Same G5 violation as X06 with a much smaller symptom; pairs with X06 to measure whether the gate honors the DEGREE bound as stated or silently re-derives its own error tolerance from the magnitude.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever beam, length 0.2 m, width 0.05 m, height 0.10 m (length/height = 2), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=1000 N, mesh_density=16, element_degree=2. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: length/height = 2 -- far below the G1 bound. Shear deformation dominates; the Euler-Bernoulli reference is the WRONG reference, so the 3D solve deflects more than the beam limit and is not validated against it.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a Timoshenko or full elasticity reference (e.g. Timoshenko & Goodier's end-loaded cantilever solution), against which this same 3D solve could be validated
gate_cases.label_rationale: G1 excludes trust below L/h = 10; the FE number may be fine but the card's only validation reference does not apply, so it cannot be endorsed as validated.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever beam, length 1.0 m, width 0.05 m, height 0.05 m (length/height = 20), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=50000 N, mesh_density=16, element_degree=2. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: The linear prediction is delta ~ 0.152 m, i.e. delta/L ~ 15%, above the G2 bound of 10%. The small-deflection solve ignores geometric stiffening, so it over-predicts deflection while converging cleanly.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a geometrically nonlinear (large-deflection) solve, which this instrument does not provide
gate_cases.label_rationale: G2 excludes trust past delta/L = 0.10; the physics assumption itself is broken, and no re-run of THIS instrument fixes it -- which is why defer is as apt as refine.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever beam, length 1.0 m, width 0.05 m, height 0.05 m (length/height = 20), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.4999, tip_load=1000 N, mesh_density=16, element_degree=2. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: nu = 0.4999 is a VALID input (passes _validate_input, < 0.5) but near-incompressible: VOLUMETRIC locking risk, which degree 2 does NOT fix. A different disease from the degree-1 shear locking of X06/X07.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a mixed/u-p or selective-reduced-integration formulation built for near-incompressibility, which this instrument does not provide
gate_cases.label_rationale: The input is well-formed so this is NOT a setup_error; the card names nu -> 0.5 volumetric locking as a numerics failure mode that degree 2 does not cure, so the converged number is suspect and trust is excluded.

wrapper_cases.note: Negative Young's modulus is nonphysical; rejected at _validate_input before any container call, no solve, no QoI.
wrapper_cases.label_rationale: The typed input's positivity rule names the offending field, so the rejection string is stable enough to assert on.

wrapper_cases.note: A zero-height beam has no cross-section; rejected at validation.
wrapper_cases.label_rationale: Zero is caught by the same positivity rule as a negative value; asserts the boundary is exclusive, not merely sign-checked.

wrapper_cases.note: nu >= 0.5 is nonphysical for an isotropic elastic solid; rejected at validation. Contrast X10: nu=0.4999 is VALID input and reaches the gate.
wrapper_cases.label_rationale: Pairs with X10 to draw the line between a nonphysical input (rejected by code) and a physical-but-suspect one (judged by the gate).

wrapper_cases.note: Exercises the NEW field. Degree 0 is not a displacement element at all, so it is a TYPED rejection. Note the deliberate asymmetry: degree 1 IS accepted (it is a regime judgment for the gate, ruling G5), while degree 0 is rejected here in code.
wrapper_cases.label_rationale: The only wrapper case exercising element_degree; it pins the typed floor (>=1) as distinct from the validated floor (>=2), which is the gate's job, not the wrapper's.

wrapper_cases.reason_substring: unsupported field(s) for fenicsx cantilever v1: material
wrapper_cases.note: `material` is not a family-v1 field; the typed input rejects unknown keys BY NAME rather than silently ignoring them.
wrapper_cases.label_rationale: Silently ignoring an unknown field would let a case believe it specified a material it did not; the rejection must name the offender.
